steps.ask: What value must g′(x) take at a turning point, and can this expression ever take that value?
steps.title: Explain why there are no turning points

lines.text: A turning point needs $\hl{1}{g'(x)} = 0$, but the numerator is $-6$, which is never $0$.
Also $(2x-7)^2 > 0$ for every $x$ in the domain ($x \ne 3.5$), so $\hl{1}{g'(x)} < 0$ always.
So $\hl{1}{g'(x)} \ne 0$ for all $x$ in the domain: $g$ has no local maximum or minimum points.

problems.final: \hl{1}{g'(x)} = -\frac{6}{(2x-7)^2} < 0 \text{ for all } x \text{ in the domain, so } \hl{4}{\text{there are no turning points}}
